items.prompt: I'm trying to give up sugar, so I've stopped ___ it in my tea.

explanation.en: Stop + -ing means give up an activity.

optionNotes.en: Stop + to would mean stopping in order to put sugar in.
The base form cannot follow stopped.

items.prompt: Please remember ___ the office before you leave tonight.

explanation.en: Remember + to-infinitive is about something you must do.
explanation.es: Remember to = no olvidar hacer algo.

optionNotes.en: Remember + -ing is a memory of the past, which does not fit before you leave.

items.prompt: I'll never forget ___ the sunrise from the top of Mount Teide.

explanation.en: Forget + -ing refers to a memory of a past experience.

optionNotes.en: Forget + to-infinitive means failing to do something.
Correct: a memory of a past experience.
The base form cannot follow forget.

items.prompt: I regret ___ so rudely to the waiter; he didn't deserve it.

explanation.en: Regret + -ing expresses sorrow about a past action.

optionNotes.en: Regret + to-infinitive is for announcing bad news formally.
The base form cannot follow regret.

items.prompt: I forgot ___ the invoice, so the client never received it.

explanation.en: Forget + to-infinitive means you did not do it. The client never received it.
explanation.es: Forgot to send = no lo envié.

optionNotes.en: Forget + -ing means you did it but cannot recall it, which contradicts the sentence.
